title: Exercise file
description: All exercises for one lesson. A lesson's exercise-group sections pull items out of here by id, so one file serves the practice, reading, dialogue and writing groups. Every exercise type engine/lessons.js renders gates the Continue button: the learner must answer correctly, and three wrong attempts reveal the answer and release the gate (MAX_ATTEMPTS). The one exception is error-correction, which lessons.js does not render at all yet — see its own description.

lesson.description: Owning lesson, e.g. a1-01. A unit split into several lessons adds a third segment, e.g. a1-01-01, a1-01-consolidation. The unit segment is a word instead of a number only where a number would collide with another unit's old lesson slot, e.g. a1-cafe-01.

id.description: Referenced by a lesson's exerciseRefs. Must be unique within the file.

category.description: What the exercise is testing. Informational; the lesson decides placement.

teaches.description: Concepts this exercise tests, as lowercase hyphenated slugs taken from the lesson's Grammar column or Vocabulary Theme in guides/a1.md. Presence of this tag is what makes an exercise eligible for the recycle block in a later lesson, so keep slugs consistent — 'ser' tagged in Lesson 1 is what lets Lesson 5 recycle it. Omit it on reading exercises: they ask about one specific story and only make sense to a learner who has just read it. See guides/a1-srs-srategy.md.

matching.description: Tap a Spanish item, then its translation. Both columns are shuffled on render. Solved when every pair is matched; on failure the full pair list is revealed.

pairs.description: Each pair is [spanish, english]. Keep to about six — every pair is on screen at once.

multipleChoice.description: One question, one right option. On failure the correct option is highlighted.

correct.description: Zero-based index into options. Options render in the order given, so this must point at the right one.

fillBlank.description: Type the missing word. Answers are compared with accents and punctuation stripped and case ignored, so 'soy' matches 'Soy'. On failure the answer is filled in.

sentence.description: The blank is two or more underscores, replaced by a placeholder on render.

sentenceBuilder.description: Assemble a sentence from shuffled word tiles. On failure the finished sentence is shown.

tiles.description: Shuffled on render. Two tiles have only one sensible arrangement, so use at least three.

solution.description: The tiles in the right order. Must contain exactly the same strings as tiles.

english.description: What the sentence means. Shown only after the learner has settled the sentence — on screen beforehand it turns building into translating.

sentenceOrder.description: Put sentences into sequence. On failure the correct order is listed out.

solution.description: Indices into sentences, in the right order. Writing them in order already means [0, 1, 2, ...].

dialogueComplete.description: An exchange with one line missing; pick the line that fits. On failure the correct option is highlighted.

prompt.description: The exchange as shown. Exactly one line's text is the blank.

text.description: Use underscores for the line the learner supplies.

substitution.description: Swap one word into a base sentence and see the result — a pattern drill, not a graded question, same as structured-writing: tapping each option reveals its resulting sentence, and Continue unlocks once every option has been seen. Added specifically for Hungarian's case/agreement marking: the swapped-in word is rarely just dropped in bare ('tejet', not 'tej'), so content supplies each option's ALREADY-inflected form and the full resulting sentence — engine/lessons.js never generates or inflects Hungarian itself, only bolds the literal substring given in `inflected`/`word` within `sentence` (highlightWord() in engine/lessons.js). A `base_word`/`inflected` value that isn't a verbatim substring of its sentence just renders with nothing bolded, not an error — but defeats the point of the exercise. No Spanish content uses this as of this writing.

base_word.description: The word being swapped, in its EXACT inflected form as it appears in base_sentence — must be a verbatim substring of it, since that's what gets bolded on render.

base_gloss.description: English translation of base_sentence, shown as a hint underneath it.

word.description: The replacement word's citation/dictionary form — shown on the option button, and used for bolding in `sentence` if `inflected` is omitted.

inflected.description: The replacement word's EXACT inflected form as it appears in `sentence`. Required whenever it differs from `word` — almost always, for Hungarian.

sentence.description: base_sentence with the word swapped in, written out in full and already grammatically correct — the whole point of this exercise is that it is NOT a naive text substitution.

gloss.description: English for the replacement word, shown next to it on the option button.

errorCorrection.description: A Spanish sentence containing one deliberate mistake; the learner retypes it correctly. Checked the same way as fill-blank — accents/punctuation/case-insensitive comparison against `solution`. Not yet rendered by engine/lessons.js — only Workshop's Grammar Driller (engine/drills/grammar-runner.js) supports this type today, so do not reference it from a lesson's exercise-group until lessons.js gains a renderer for it.

sentence.description: The Spanish sentence as given, containing exactly one mistake.

explanation.description: Shown after the learner answers, right or wrong — what was wrong and why.

structuredWriting.description: Free writing against English prompts. There is no single right answer, so nothing is marked: once every line has text the learner presses Check, each model answer appears beneath their own sentence to compare against, and Continue unlocks.

template.description: One entry per line the learner writes. Prompt and model answer are kept together so they cannot drift apart.

answer.description: One natural way to say it, shown as an example rather than as the correct answer. Use only grammar and vocabulary the lesson has taught.

listeningChoice.description: Audio plays a Spanish sentence, with no Spanish text on screen; the learner picks its meaning from English options. Reuses the multiple-choice interaction — engine/lessons.js renders `sentence` as a play button instead of visible text. On failure the correct option is highlighted, same as multiple-choice.

sentence.description: The Spanish read aloud. Never shown as text — only spoken, via the browser's speechSynthesis.

options.description: English meanings. Exactly one matches what was said.

dictation.description: Audio plays a Spanish sentence; the learner types what they heard. Checked the same way as fill-blank: accents, punctuation and case are ignored.

sentence.description: The Spanish read aloud and the expected answer. Never shown as text before the learner answers.
